title: Fourteen Years and One Unpaid Page
subtitle: 经济与消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济与消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济与消费（社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：debt　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 debt 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 my grandfather ① owed a debt that no banker in the town would have carried, and he said the owing was the whole of the shop. The ② debt, meaning the money and not the obligation, ran fourteen years and stayed unentered in the book; a debt, he said, is the only thing in a ledger that is judged by how long it is left unpaid.

Every ③ debt in that book had the same unpaid page against it, and the ④ debt at the end, meaning the one he kept for the widows and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever forgave twice. A debt, my grandmother said, is nine parts name and one part somebody willing to wait; my grandfather said the waiting is the part that fills fourteen years.

The accountant meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the debt was the whole of the account, meaning the obligation and not the money. The ⑥ debt, meaning the obligation and not any of that, is the only thing in an account that everybody enters and nobody forgives; debt, he said, is either something you owe or the only word that means both a money and an obligation. He said the obligation is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ debt had become a line in a statement, and the statement had become an argument about the unpaid page. The ⑧ debt of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in May, was one shop and fourteen years of waiting; debt, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to wait. She said the waiting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ debt I remember is the one at the end, which was settled in 1975 and is still described as the oldest in the town. A ⑩ debt, my grandmother said in 1977, is the only thing that improves by being forgiven; every debt, she said, is an obligation that has agreed to look like a money. She said the obligation was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 债务；欠款（指账簿上记着的那一笔）
B. n. 欠款（指那笔钱本身，与那份义务相对）
C. 固定搭配：owe a debt 欠一笔债
D. n. 债务（指他为寡妇们留着的那一笔）
E. n. 债务；欠账（抽象总称，指一家店的全部赊欠）
F. n. 债务（指结算单上写到、被列明的那一笔）
G. n. 债务；义务（指账户上那份须偿的义务）
H. n. 义务（抽象总称，指人人入账却无人免除的那一份）

items.q: owed a debt that no banker in the town would have carried
The debt, meaning the money and not the obligation
the debt was the whole of the account
the debt had become a line in a statement
The debt of the whole thing
A debt, my grandmother said in 1977

answers.why: owe a debt 意为“欠一笔债”，1957 年祖父欠了一笔全镇没有一位银行家肯承担的债。
debt 意为“欠款”，指那笔钱本身而不是那份义务，它在账簿里挂了十四年而没有入账。
debt 意为“债务”，指那本账簿里每一笔债务，每一笔都对着同一页未付的记录。
debt 意为“债务”，指他为寡妇们留着的那一笔，是唯一有人免除过两次的。
debt 意为“债务、义务”，指账户上那份须偿的义务，会计说这份义务就是那个账户的全部。
debt 意为“义务”，指人人入账却无人免除的那一份而不是那笔钱，是账户里人人都入账、却无人免除的东西。
debt 意为“债务”，指结算单上写到、被列明的那一笔，到 1964 年这笔债成了结算单里的一行。
debt 意为“债务、欠账”，祖父五月写道，整件事的欠账是一家店铺和十四年的等待。
debt 意为“债务”，我记得的是末尾那一笔，1975 年结清，至今仍被说成全镇最久的一笔。
debt 为抽象总称，祖母 1977 年说，一笔债务是唯一会因为被免除而变得更好的东西。
